title: A Regional Dengue Response Under Uncertainty

fiction_notice.statement: This case is entirely invented training material. The Republic of Mereva, Kerrin Region, every settlement, facility, body, office, document, figure and currency unit named here does not exist and resembles no actual jurisdiction, institution, dataset or event. No real outbreak, no real statute, no real circular, no real official and no real price appears anywhere in this case or in its source register.
fiction_notice.as_of_date_meaning: The in-world date on which the briefing reaches the user. It is not a real-world currency claim about anything.
fiction_notice.not_a_forecast: Anything the exercise narrates as a consequence is a teaching device and never an empirical forecast (PRD 8.3).

editorial_boundary.rule: Guyana-first is editorial context, not license to invent Guyanese legal provisions, institutional positions, budgets, prices or health data (canon 1.2, PRD 9.4, FR-08).
how_this_case_complies: The jurisdiction is invented. No real region, town, hospital, body or official is named.

No statute, regulation, circular, instrument number or legal provision is named, invented or cited - not even a fictional one. Legal authority appears only as a question the user must verify and as two in-scenario officials disagreeing about it.

No epidemiological or clinical fact about dengue as a disease appears in the register. Stating one would require either a real citation, which is prohibited here, or an invented health fact, which is worse. Clinical management is out of scope for the role this case asks the user to play.
Every money figure is denominated in an invented in-scenario currency unit (ISU) so that no number can be read as a real budget or price.
Every source is an in-scenario document authored with the case, labeled as such in its own title and publisher, and carrying kind 'fictional_assumption' in the database.

learning_objective: Set first-72-hour priorities when two surveillance instruments disagree, the authority to restrict movement is believed but unverified, and every resource that could be moved is already committed to something else; identify explicitly what must be verified before acting; allocate finite testing and transport capacity with the trade-off stated; and communicate uncertainty without either minimizing risk or causing alarm.

jurisdiction.name: Kerrin Region, Republic of Mereva
jurisdiction.description: A low-lying coastal and riverine region of an invented tropical state, with three districts: Kerrin East (coastal, containing the regional town of Pellon), Kerrin West (agricultural), and Kerrin Interior (riverine and forested, reachable mainly by boat).
settlements: Pellon - regional town, Kerrin East, in-world population estimate 41,000 (2019 in-world estimate)
Dray Hill - farming village, Kerrin West
Sabaka Landing - riverine village cluster, Kerrin Interior
Three Creeks - interior settlement, Kerrin Interior
facilities: Kerrin Regional Hospital, Pellon - 18 inpatient beds, 7 clinical staff
Sabaka Landing Health Post - staffed until 14:00, no overnight cover
Three Creeks Health Post - roof repair deferred
bodies: Office of the National Coordinating Executive - the user's office
jurisdiction.people: Every person in this case appears by role only. No name, real or invented, is attached to any position, so no one can be impersonated and no invented official can be mistaken for a real one.

issue_statement: Kerrin Region has reported a rising number of suspected dengue cases over two weeks. Two counting instruments disagree and the regional surveillance desk has not reconciled them. Laboratory confirmation exists for a small minority of suspected cases and the only confirmatory route runs through the national laboratory with a five-to-seven-day turnaround. The regional health authority has asked for an immediate movement restriction on one riverine village; the coordinating office's own legal adviser has asked for written confirmation of the power to issue such an order and reports that none has been located. The two river boats that could carry testing and staff into the interior are already committed, one of them to a school-feeding run the affected community was told would continue. A regional radio station has asked for a statement by midday tomorrow, a public statement issued four days ago described testing capacity as adequate, and a claim that the rapid tests cause the illness is circulating in two of the three districts. An interagency call reconvenes in-world 8 March at 18:00 and expects an interim 72-hour plan.

user_role.title: National coordinating executive for a simulated interagency response
user_role.authority_in_scenario: Chairs the interagency response, directs the coordinating office, and tables the 72-hour plan at the next national call.
explicit_limits: The user is not a clinician and the case supplies no clinical guidance; clinical management is out of scope.
Whether the user may authorize a movement restriction is one of the unknowns of the case, not a power the case grants.
The user cannot create capacity. Every allocation in this case takes something from somewhere named.

decision_window.interim_milestone: An interim 72-hour plan is tabled at the interagency call at 18:00 on in-world 8 March.
decision_window.nearest_external_pressure: A regional radio station has asked for a statement by 12:00 on in-world 7 March, which falls 29 hours into the window.

available_resources: 1,100 rapid tests in regional stock, of which 300 reach their marked expiry within 6 weeks
Regional laboratory throughput of 40 rapid tests per day at current staffing, with 1 of 3 technicians on leave until in-world 12 March
A confirmatory testing route through the national laboratory with a 5-to-7-day turnaround and 212 samples already awaiting dispatch
2 serviceable river boats assigned to Kerrin Interior, with fuel on hand for 11 days of one daily run
Larvicide sufficient for 40 percent of the 96 identified breeding sites, and 2 of 3 serviceable sprayer units
A regional contingency line of 18,400,000 ISU for the current quarter
7 clinical staff at the regional hospital, 2 of them on leave; a request for 4 relief staff is unanswered after 6 days
A community liaison desk with existing contacts in Sabaka Landing and Three Creeks
fictional_assumptions: Assumption: the Republic of Mereva, Kerrin Region, its three districts, four settlements, five facilities and six bodies are invented for this exercise and correspond to nothing real.

Assumption: every figure in this case - case counts, test stock, throughput, bed numbers, staffing, distances, journey times, breeding-site counts, rainfall comparisons and money - was chosen to create a specific decision tension and is not drawn from any real dataset, register or budget.
Assumption: the currency is the in-scenario currency unit (ISU), which has no exchange rate and no real-world equivalent.
Assumption: all ten documents in the source register were written as part of this case. None is a copy, summary or paraphrase of any real document.
Assumption: the in-world calendar runs 1 March to 9 March 2026 and the dates on the documents are in-world dates.

Assumption: the case supplies no clinical, epidemiological or vector-biology guidance, and the user is not expected to supply any. A response that reasons clinically is reasoning outside the material the case provides.

Assumption: the legal position is deliberately unresolved. The case contains no statute, no instrument and no authoritative statement of who may restrict movement, because inventing one would teach a false certainty.
Assumption: the two disagreeing case counts are both reported in good faith inside the scenario. The case does not reveal which is closer to the in-world truth, and no later document resolves it.
data_gaps: Laboratory confirmation is absent for 153 of the 184 suspected cases in situation report 3.
The Sabaka Landing Health Post tally and the district figures have not been reconciled, and situation report 4 marks its own totals unvalidated.
The surveillance form in Kerrin West and Kerrin Interior does not capture patient residence, so cases cannot be located below district level.
The only population denominator available to the surveillance desk is an in-world 2019 estimate.
The cause of 2 of the 3 deaths under review is recorded as undetermined.
No written confirmation of the power to restrict movement has been located by the coordinating office.
No decision has been taken on the request for 4 relief clinical staff, 6 days after it was made.
The rainfall comparison is against the environmental health desk's own log and no other record.
Nothing in the register establishes how many of the 96 suspected cases in the health post tally were also counted in the district figures.

conflicting_evidence.summary: Two counting instruments disagree about Sabaka Landing, and both are in the register.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: The district figure of 38 and the health post tally of 96 cannot both describe the same population over overlapping periods. Which one the user acts on changes where testing and transport go, and the case never resolves it. A response that silently picks one has made an assumption it has not stated.

conflicting_evidence.summary: The number of deaths attributable to the outbreak is reported two different ways.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: Three deaths under review and one death attributed with two undetermined are different public statements. The communication decision turns on which is said out loud and with what qualification.

conflicting_evidence.summary: Testing capacity looks sufficient by stock and insufficient by turnaround.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: 1,100 tests in stock reads as adequate. 40 tests a day, 212 samples queued for a 5-to-7-day confirmatory route and 300 tests near expiry read as a capacity that cannot answer the question in the decision window. Both pictures are sourced.

conflicting_evidence.summary: The same river boat is committed twice.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: The transport memo lists two serviceable boats as available. The community liaison note records that one of them was promised to a school-feeding run. Using it for testing breaks a commitment to the settlement that is furthest from care.

conflicting_evidence.summary: The authority to restrict movement is asserted from practice and denied in writing.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: One official says the region has done this before. The coordinating office's legal adviser says no written confirmation of the power has been found and asks for it before anything is signed. A third official says any restriction would be announced nationally. The case deliberately contains no instrument, so the only defensible move is to name what must be verified and by whom.

conflicting_evidence.summary: The contingency line can fund the two operational asks or protect the deferred roof repair, but not both within the practice threshold.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: The line holds 18,400,000 ISU. Sixty percent of it is 11,040,000 ISU, above which drawings have previously been returned for written justification. An extra daily river run for 30 days costs 2,700,000 ISU and 4 relief staff for 30 days cost 6,900,000 ISU, together 9,600,000 ISU. Adding the 4,100,000 ISU roof repair reaches 13,700,000 ISU and crosses the threshold. The arithmetic is checkable and the trade-off is real.

conflicting_evidence.summary: The last public statement is contradicted by the laboratory note, and two stakeholders disagree about whether to speak at all.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: A statement four days old described capacity as adequate. The radio station wants something by midday. The national disaster unit wants nothing said regionally before the next call. A claim that the tests cause the illness is already circulating. Saying nothing, repeating the old line, and correcting it all have costs that the register supports.

conflicting_evidence.summary: Three stakeholders want the same scarce capacity for three different purposes.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: All rapid tests to Kerrin East, rapid tests reserved for hospital presentations, and vector control ahead of testing are each defensible and mutually exclusive at this capacity. There is no allocation that satisfies all three, so the user must choose and say why.

conflicting_evidence.summary: Containment and access point in opposite directions for the same community.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: The restriction that the regional authority wants would close the only route Sabaka Landing has to the hospital and to the market, from a health post with no cover after 14:00. Both positions are legitimate and the register grounds both.

conflicting_evidence.summary: A measure intended to find cases may reduce the reporting the measure depends on.
conflicting_evidence.why_it_matters: Residents told the liaison desk they would be less willing to present if presenting could trigger a restriction, against a background of an outreach promise met 3 times in 11 weeks. The second-order effect runs against the first-order aim.

stakeholders.position: Restrict movement to and from Sabaka Landing immediately and move all rapid-test capacity to Kerrin East, where most suspected cases are recorded.
stakeholders.legitimate_interest: Accountable for the region's case numbers and working from the only district-level figures that exist.

stakeholders.position: Reserve rapid tests for patients presenting at the hospital and send no outreach team into the interior until relief staff arrive.
stakeholders.legitimate_interest: Responsible for the patients already in front of them, with 2 of 7 clinical staff on leave and 4 of 18 beds free.

stakeholders.role: Representative, national finance desk, National Health Coordination Office
stakeholders.position: No drawing on the contingency line without a written justification, and the Three Creeks roof commitment is to be protected.
stakeholders.legitimate_interest: Stewardship of a single quarterly line that has already been promised to a deferred repair.

stakeholders.position: Oppose a movement restriction while the river route is the only link to the hospital and to the district market.
stakeholders.legitimate_interest: The restriction's whole cost falls on them, and the route is their access to both care and income.

stakeholders.position: Restore the promised weekly outreach visit before any new regional measure, and do not take the school-feeding boat.
stakeholders.legitimate_interest: Furthest from care, 210 minutes from the hospital, with an outreach promise met 3 times in 11 weeks.

stakeholders.position: Prioritize vector control over additional testing and issue no regional public statement before the next national call.
stakeholders.legitimate_interest: Owns national message discipline and reads the rainfall and breeding-site picture as the driver.

stakeholders.position: Asking for a statement by 12:00 on in-world 7 March and reporting the circulating claim about the tests either way.
stakeholders.legitimate_interest: An audience that is already hearing the rumor and a previous official statement that said capacity was adequate.

legal_authority.how_this_case_states_it: As an unresolved question, never as a provision. No statute, regulation, instrument or legal citation appears anywhere in this case, fictional or otherwise.
legal_authority.what_the_user_faces: The regional health authority asserts that movement has been restricted this way before. The coordinating office's legal adviser has asked for written confirmation of the power before any order is signed and reports that none has been located. The national disaster unit says any restriction would be announced nationally rather than regionally. The minute records no decision and lists the question as outstanding for the coordinating executive.
legal_authority.what_a_strong_response_does: Names the restriction as an action requiring verified authority, states who must confirm it and in what form, says what will be done in the meantime, and does not assert a power it cannot evidence.
legal_authority.what_a_weak_response_does: Asserts or implies an authority, or cites a provision. Any provision cited against this case is fabricated, because the case contains none.

budgetary.currency: ISU (in-scenario currency unit, invented, no real-world equivalent)
budgetary.practice_threshold_note: Drawings above 60 percent of the line in a single quarter, that is above 11,040,000 ISU, have previously been returned by the national finance desk for written justification. This is recorded in the case as a past practice of an invented body, not as a rule of law.
costed_options: Additional daily river run, 30 days: 2,700,000 ISU
Three Creeks Health Post roof repair, already promised against this line: 4,100,000 ISU

required_decision: Define the priorities for the first 72 hours and say what is deliberately not being done.
Identify the decision authority that must be verified before a movement restriction could be issued, and state how it will be verified and by when.
Allocate the rapid tests, the laboratory throughput, the two river boats and the contingency line, naming what each allocation displaces.
Specify the communication approach, including what will be said about the two disagreeing counts, the deaths under review and the circulating claim about the tests.
State the safeguards for the communities that bear the cost of whatever is decided, in particular Sabaka Landing and Three Creeks.
response_template: 4. Assumptions made and data still missing
6. Equity and legal-authority checks, including what must be verified
8. Indicators and a stated forecast with a timeframe
second_order_effects: A movement restriction may reduce willingness to present at the health post, degrading the surveillance the restriction is meant to inform (C-REPORTING-BEHAVIOUR).

Moving the school-feeding boat to testing duty breaks a stated commitment to the settlement furthest from care, with a liaison relationship already weakened by an outreach promise met 3 times in 11 weeks (C-TRANSPORT-DOUBLE-COMMIT, C-OUTREACH-SHORTFALL).
Drawing the contingency line for operations defers the Three Creeks roof repair into the wetter weeks the environmental log already records (C-ROOF-COMMITMENT, C-RAINFALL-LOG).
Concentrating rapid tests in Kerrin East leaves the interior counted by the instrument the surveillance desk has marked unvalidated (C-POS-KRHA, C-COUNT-CONFLICT).

Repeating the earlier 'capacity is adequate' line and later correcting it costs more trust than qualifying it now, and the rumor about the tests is already circulating in two districts (C-PRIOR-STATEMENT, C-RUMOUR-TESTS).

Sending samples into a 212-sample queue with a 5-to-7-day turnaround produces confirmations after the decision window closes, so the plan tabled at the national call will still rest on suspected counts (C-LAB-BACKLOG, C-LAB-CONFIRMATORY-TURNAROUND).

Reserving all testing for hospital presentations biases the case picture toward people who can reach Pellon, which is nobody in Three Creeks within 210 minutes (C-POS-CLINICAL-LEAD, C-TRANSPORT-TRIP-TIME).

challenge_lenses.prompt: Which authority would permit the restriction you propose, and what must be verified, by whom, before it could be used?
challenge_lenses.abstention_note: The register contains no instrument and no provision. A challenge that names one has fabricated it, and the grounding whitelist cannot support it.

challenge_lenses.prompt: What is delayed or dropped when funding moves to testing and transport, and is that trade-off justified on the figures in the register?
How does your plan avoid disadvantaging the communities with the least access, and who bears the cost of the measure you chose?
What is the fallback if confirmatory results are delayed past the decision window, and which of your steps depends on a resource that is already committed?
How will you communicate what is not yet known without either minimizing the risk or causing alarm, given what was already said publicly?

claim_register.claim_text: Situation report 3 records 184 suspected cases across Kerrin Region for the 14 days ending in-world 3 March, of which 131 are in Kerrin East.
Situation report 3 attributes 38 of the 184 suspected cases to Sabaka Landing and 15 to Three Creeks.
Situation report 3 records laboratory confirmation for 31 of the 184 suspected cases, leaving 153 unconfirmed.
Situation report 3 records 1 death attributed to the outbreak and 2 further deaths whose cause is recorded as undetermined.
Situation report 3 uses a regional population estimate dated in-world 2019 and states that no later estimate is available to the surveillance desk.
Situation report 4 lists 3 deaths under review in Kerrin Region for the reporting period and does not state how they relate to the deaths in situation report 3.
Situation report 4 states that the surveillance desk has not reconciled the Sabaka Landing Health Post tally with the district figures, and marks its own totals unvalidated.
Situation report 4 states that the surveillance form in use in Kerrin West and Kerrin Interior does not capture patient residence, so cases cannot be located below district level.
The Sabaka Landing Health Post handwritten tally records 96 suspected cases seen at the post in the 9 days ending in-world 5 March.
The regional laboratory reports a sustainable throughput of 40 rapid tests per day at current staffing.
The regional laboratory holds 1,100 rapid tests in stock.
The laboratory records 300 of the 1,100 rapid tests in stock as reaching their marked expiry within 6 weeks.
Confirmatory testing is performed only at the national laboratory, and the regional laboratory records a turnaround of 5 to 7 days for samples sent there.
The regional laboratory reports 212 samples awaiting dispatch to the national laboratory.
The laboratory records 1 of its 3 technicians on approved leave until in-world 12 March.
The Regional Transport Pool lists 2 serviceable river boats assigned to Kerrin Interior and records no other river transport available to the region.
The transport memo records fuel on hand for 11 days of one daily river run.
The contingency note records 18,400,000 ISU available in the regional contingency line for the current quarter.

The contingency note records that drawings above 60 percent of the line in a single quarter, that is above 11,040,000 ISU, have previously been returned by the national finance desk for written justification. The note describes this as past practice and cites no rule.
The contingency note records the same line as the only identified funding for the deferred Three Creeks Health Post roof repair, costed at 4,100,000 ISU.
The contingency note costs an additional daily river run for 30 days at 2,700,000 ISU including fuel and crew.
The contingency note costs 4 relief clinical staff for 30 days at 6,900,000 ISU and records that no decision on the request has been taken.

In the coordination call the regional health authority's representative stated that the region had restricted movement to and from a riverine village on an earlier occasion and that the same route would be used again. The minute records no instrument, provision or written basis for that statement.

The minute records the coordinating office's legal adviser asking for written confirmation of the power to restrict movement before any order is signed, and states that no written confirmation of that power has been located by the office.
The minute records the national disaster unit's liaison stating that any movement restriction would be announced nationally rather than regionally, and the regional representative disagreeing.
The minute records no decision on who may issue a movement restriction and lists the question as outstanding for the coordinating executive.
In the coordination call the regional health authority's director asked for an immediate movement restriction on Sabaka Landing and for all rapid-test capacity to be moved to Kerrin East.
The regional hospital's clinical lead asked that rapid tests be reserved for patients presenting at the hospital and that relief staff arrive before any outreach expansion.

The national finance desk's representative stated that no drawing on the contingency line would be processed without a written justification, and asked that the Three Creeks roof commitment be protected.
The national disaster unit's liaison asked that vector control be prioritized over additional testing and that no regional public statement be issued before the next national call.
The clinical lead reported 2 of the regional hospital's 7 clinical staff on leave, and a request for 4 relief staff with the national office for 6 days without reply.
The clinical lead reported 4 of the regional hospital's 18 inpatient beds unoccupied at the time of the call.
The minute records the next interagency call at 18:00 on in-world 8 March, with an interim 72-hour plan to be tabled.
The field note records a 210-minute boat journey from Three Creeks to the regional hospital at Pellon and no alternative route.
The field note records that residents of Three Creeks were told one of the two river boats would continue the weekly school-feeding run.
The field note records that a weekly outreach visit promised to Three Creeks was made 3 times in the past 11 weeks.
The field note records that the Sabaka Landing Health Post is staffed until 14:00 and has no overnight cover.
The field note records the Sabaka Landing river route as the only link residents have to the district market they use for income and supplies.
The field note records residents saying they would be less willing to present at the health post if presenting could lead to a movement restriction.
Sabaka Landing's community representatives told the liaison desk they would oppose a movement restriction while the river route remains their only link to the hospital and to the market.
Three Creeks' community representatives asked that the outreach visit be restored before any new regional measure, and said regional attention follows the coastal district.
The stock count records larvicide sufficient for 40 percent of the 96 breeding sites identified in the region.
The stock count records 1 of 3 sprayer units unserviceable and awaiting a part.
The environmental health desk's own log records rainfall above the region's recorded seasonal pattern in 3 of the past 4 weeks. The log is the only record cited for that comparison.

The public information log records a circulating claim that the rapid tests cause the illness, reported from 2 of the region's 3 districts. The log records it as a circulating claim and offers no assessment of it.
The public information log records a statement issued in-world 2 March describing regional testing capacity as adequate.
The public information log records a regional radio station's request for a statement by 12:00 on in-world 7 March.

rubric.reference: PRD 7.1 five assessment dimensions, 7.2 maturity levels, 7.3 formative decision-quality rubric. Stored in public.rubric_version and pinned by this scenario_version.
hard_rules_restated: No composite readiness, character or viability score, ever (canon 1.2).
An AI assessor may not record an observed level above 2, enforced by a database CHECK, not by prompt text.
Observed level is always displayed with evidence quality, assessor kind and review date.

source_verification.reason: PRD 8.2's source-verification stage exists to verify external sources. This case cites none: every entry in the source register is an in-scenario document authored with the case and carries kind 'fictional_assumption'. There is nothing external to verify, and that is the point rather than a gap.

subject_matter_and_ethics_review.reason: No subject-matter or ethics review has taken place. No reviewer name and no sign-off date is recorded here, because canon 12.3 forbids inventing one. Until that record exists and is referenced, this leg is outstanding and should be treated as a release-gate item for the pilot, not as discharged.

exclusions: No statute, regulation, circular, instrument, provision or legal citation - real or invented - appears in this case.
No real institution, agency, dataset, publication, DOI or URL is cited. The source register contains no uri at all.
No named person, real or invented. Every participant appears by role.
No clinical, epidemiological or vector-biology guidance, and no claim about dengue as a disease.
